tasks.title: Sec A · 第 1 组
tasks.context: Questions 1 to 4 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: What is the man planning to do?

options.A: Celebrate his 10th wedding anniversary.
options.B: Celebrate his promotion in Barcelona.
options.C: Give his wife a pleasant surprise.
options.D: Ask for leave to visit Barcelona.

questions.cn: 男士打算做什么？

optionsCn.A: 庆祝他结婚十周年。
optionsCn.B: 庆祝他在巴塞罗那的升职。
optionsCn.C: 给妻子一个惊喜。
optionsCn.D: 请假去巴塞罗那游玩。

questions.stem: Why is the man starting to feel a bit frantic?

options.A: He is unable to find some inexpensive accommodation.
options.B: There are few warm places to go at this time of the year.
options.C: There is so much for him to do before going on vacation.
options.D: He is afraid Barcelona may not be so fabulous as expected.

questions.cn: 男士为什么开始感到有些抓狂？

optionsCn.A: 他找不到价格合适的住处。
optionsCn.B: 一年中的这个时候可去的暖和地方很少。
optionsCn.C: 度假前他要做的事太多了。
optionsCn.D: 他担心巴塞罗那可能没有想象中那么好。

questions.stem: What does the woman suggest the man do?

options.A: Rent a car to drive into the city and scenic spots so as to save the expenses on transportation.
options.B: Spend a couple of nights in a glamorous hotel and the rest of the week in inexpensive places.
options.C: Find all-inclusive accommodation to eliminate the need to pay for food and drinks.
options.D: Stay in a hotel away from the coast where the accommodation is less expensive.

questions.cn: 女士建议男士怎么做？

optionsCn.A: 租车进城和去景点，以节省交通开支。
optionsCn.B: 在一家高档酒店住两晚，其余几天住便宜的地方。
optionsCn.C: 找包三餐的住宿，省下吃饭喝饮料的钱。
optionsCn.D: 住在远离海岸、住宿更便宜的酒店。

questions.stem: What does the man say about his wife Jane?

options.A: She is sure to like the cathedral.
options.B: She is a romantic at heart.
options.C: She is no good at logistics.
options.D: She is scared of heights.

questions.cn: 关于妻子简，男士说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 她肯定会喜欢那座大教堂。
optionsCn.B: 她骨子里很浪漫。
optionsCn.C: 她不擅长安排行程。
optionsCn.D: 她恐高。

lines.t: F: Hi Frank, are you working through your lunch hour again?
lines.cn: F：嗨，弗兰克，你又一边吃午饭一边干活呢？

lines.t: M: No, not at all.
lines.cn: M：没有，完全没有。

lines.t: M: It's my 10th wedding anniversary next week and I promised Jane that I would book a city break for us as I have annual leave to take and it would be nice to celebrate somewhere warm, so I'm trying to book something in Barcelona.
lines.cn: M：下周是我结婚十周年纪念日，我答应过简要订一趟城市短假，因为我还有年假要休，能去个暖和的地方庆祝一下就好了，所以我正想订巴塞罗那的行程。

lines.t: F: That sounds so romantic!
lines.cn: F：听起来太浪漫了！

lines.t: F: I adore Barcelona.
lines.cn: F：我特别喜欢巴塞罗那。

lines.t: F: It's such a fabulous cosmopolitan city.
lines.cn: F：那是一座特别棒的国际大都市。

lines.t: F: There's so much to do there.
lines.cn: F：那儿可玩的东西太多了。

lines.t: F: Excellent food and that cathedral that they are still building after about 150 years.
lines.cn: F：美食一流，还有那座盖了大约 150 年还在施工的大教堂。

lines.t: F: Very cool.
lines.cn: F：太酷了。

lines.t: M: I know, but the anniversary is looming and I'm still scrambling to find accommodation.
lines.cn: M：我知道，可纪念日一天天逼近，我还在手忙脚乱地找住的地方。

lines.t: M: Everything is either wildly expensive or already fully booked.
lines.cn: M：要么贵得离谱，要么早就订满了。

lines.t: M: I'm starting to feel a bit frantic.
lines.cn: M：我开始有点抓狂了。

lines.t: F: Well, if you are going for a whole week, why don't you do a couple of nights in somewhere really glamorous and then do the rest of the week a bit further up the coast where the accommodation is cheaper and that will offset the cost of the expensive place.
lines.cn: F：那这样，既然你要去一整周，何不先在一个特别高档的地方住两晚，剩下几天住到海岸线再往上一点、住宿更便宜的地方？这样就能把贵的那家费用摊平。

lines.t: M: That might be a good plan.
lines.cn: M：这主意不错。

lines.t: M: It's not too expensive to rent a car, so we could still drive into the city.
lines.cn: M：租车也不算贵，所以我们还是可以开车进城。

lines.t: F: Yes, there are lots of places outside the city that have pools and are all inclusive, so we wouldn't even need to pay for food or drinks.
lines.cn: F：对，城外有很多带泳池、还包三餐的度假村，那样连吃饭喝饮料的钱都省了。

lines.t: M: I'll send a query now about the dates we're interested in.
lines.cn: M：我现在就发个询价，问问我们想去的那些日期。

lines.t: F: That sounds perfect.
lines.cn: F：那太好了。

lines.t: F: I'm sure that Jane will be absolutely thrilled to bits.
lines.cn: F：简肯定会高兴坏了。

lines.t: F: I really do recommend visiting that cathedral.
lines.cn: F：我真的推荐去看看那座大教堂。

lines.t: F: You can go all the way up to the top of it, but you need to go up a really steep spiral staircase to get there.
lines.cn: F：你可以一直爬到塔顶，不过得走一段特别陡的螺旋楼梯才能上去。

lines.t: M: Considering Jane is terrified of heights, I think if I tried to make her do that, I would come back divorced.
lines.cn: M：考虑到简恐高，我要是逼她爬那个，估计回来就得离婚了。

lines.t: M: Thanks for the help, though.
lines.cn: M：不过还是谢谢你的建议。

lines.t: M: It was turning into a logistical nightmare.
lines.cn: M：这事本来都快变成一场行程安排的噩梦了。

tasks.title: Sec A · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: What do we learn about the speakers?

options.A: They often share each other's experiences.
options.B: They enjoy interacting with patients.
options.C: They always do things tricky.
options.D: They are both pharmacists.

questions.cn: 关于这两位说话人，我们能了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 他们常常交流各自的经历。
optionsCn.B: 他们喜欢与患者互动。
optionsCn.C: 他们做事总是很棘手。
optionsCn.D: 他们都是药剂师。

questions.stem: What does the woman say about an interesting case she had?

options.A: The doctor ended up admitting his mistake.
options.B: The patient consulted another doctor.
options.C: The patient actually took her advice.
options.D: The doctor double-checked with her.

questions.cn: 关于她遇到的那个有意思的病例，女士说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 医生最终承认了自己的错误。
optionsCn.B: 那位病人另找了一位医生咨询。
optionsCn.C: 那位病人确实听了她的建议。
optionsCn.D: 医生和她做了核实。

questions.stem: What does the man say he has been working on?

options.A: A proposal for applying flu shots more effectively.
options.B: A new medication therapy management program.
options.C: A novel strategy to persuade stubborn patients.
options.D: A therapy for patients with similar conditions.

questions.cn: 男士说他一直在做什么？

optionsCn.A: 一项更有效接种流感疫苗的提案。
optionsCn.B: 一套新的药物治疗管理方案。
optionsCn.C: 一种说服固执病人的新策略。
optionsCn.D: 一种针对相似病症患者的疗法。

questions.stem: What is a big problem, especially for older patients, according to the woman?

options.A: Inability to send text messages.
options.B: Distrust in pharmaceutical experts.
options.C: Medication non-adherence.
options.D: Need for constant reminding.

questions.cn: 在女士看来，什么是个大问题，对老年患者尤其如此？

optionsCn.A: 不会发短信。
optionsCn.B: 不信任药学专家。
optionsCn.C: 不按医嘱服药。
optionsCn.D: 需要不断提醒。

lines.t: M: How about you?
lines.cn: M：你呢？

lines.t: F: Same here.
lines.cn: F：我也一样。

lines.t: F: Although I did have an interesting case come in this morning.
lines.cn: F：不过今天上午我这儿来了个挺有意思的病人。

lines.t: F: A patient came in, inquiring about a medication that had a potential interaction with another medication she was already taking.
lines.cn: F：一位病人来问一种药，说她正在吃的另一种药可能会和它产生相互作用。

lines.t: M: Oh, that's always tricky.
lines.cn: M：哦，这种事一向棘手。

lines.t: M: What did you do?
lines.cn: M：那你怎么处理的？

lines.t: F: I explained the issue to her as best I could, and recommended she double check with her doctor.
lines.cn: F：我尽量把问题给她讲清楚，并建议她再跟自己的医生核实一下。

lines.t: F: And you know what?
lines.cn: F：你猜怎么着？

lines.t: F: She actually followed my advice, and the doctor ended up switching the patient's medication.
lines.cn: F：她真的照我说的做了，结果医生给这位病人换了药。

lines.t: M: Ah, that's great.
lines.cn: M：啊，那太好了。

lines.t: M: You must feel quite accomplished.
lines.cn: M：你一定很有成就感。

lines.t: F: Totally.
lines.cn: F：确实。

lines.t: F: These moments are the highlights of my routine work, employing my pharmaceutical expertise to the benefit of people's health and well-being.
lines.cn: F：这些时刻就是我日常工作中最闪光的部分——用自己的药学专长，为人们的健康和福祉出力。

lines.t: M: I fully agree.
lines.cn: M：我完全同意。

lines.t: M: Unfortunately, the opposite is true when the patient is too stubborn, and they refuse to listen to us.
lines.cn: M：可惜遇上太固执、不肯听我们话的病人时，情况就正相反了。

lines.t: F: So true.
lines.cn: F：太对了。

lines.t: F: In other developments, we've had a lot of people coming in to get their flu shots, which is always good to see.
lines.cn: F：另外，最近来打流感疫苗的人很多，这是好事。

lines.t: M: Good, good.
lines.cn: M：好，好。

lines.t: M: I've been working on a new medication therapy management program for our patients with chronic conditions.
lines.cn: M：我一直在为慢性病患者做一套新的药物治疗管理方案。

lines.t: M: It helps patients manage their medications more effectively.
lines.cn: M：它能帮助患者更有效地管理自己的用药。

lines.t: F: That sounds interesting.
lines.cn: F：听起来挺有意思。

lines.t: M: We review all of their medications, and make sure that they're taking them as prescribed.
lines.cn: M：我们会把他们所有的药过一遍，确认他们是按医嘱服用的。

lines.t: M: We also look for any potential drug interactions.
lines.cn: M：我们还会排查任何潜在的药物相互作用。

lines.t: M: Patient response has so far been very positive.
lines.cn: M：到目前为止，患者的反馈非常积极。

lines.t: M: Some have reported seeing improvements in their health, which is really rewarding to see.
lines.cn: M：有些人说自己的健康状况有了改善，看到这个真的很值得。

lines.t: F: That's great to hear.
lines.cn: F：听你这么说太好了。

lines.t: F: Do you use text message reminders?
lines.cn: F：你们用短信提醒吗？

lines.t: M: Yes, absolutely.
lines.cn: M：当然用。

lines.t: F: It's a great idea.
lines.cn: F：这主意很棒。

lines.t: F: Medication non-adherence is a big problem, especially for older patients.
lines.cn: F：不按医嘱服药是个大问题，对老年患者尤其如此。

lines.t: M: We're still in the early stages of the program, but I'm hopeful that it will make a real difference for our patients.
lines.cn: M：这个方案还在早期阶段，但我希望它能真正帮到我们的患者。

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 1 组
tasks.context: Questions 9 to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: What are passionate people considered likely to do in America?

options.A: Accomplish their goals.
options.B: View things positively.
options.C: Overstate their importance.
options.D: Dominate job interviews.

questions.cn: 在美国，充满热情的人被认为很可能做到什么？

optionsCn.A: 实现他们的目标。
optionsCn.B: 积极地看待事物。
optionsCn.C: 夸大他们的重要性。
optionsCn.D: 在求职面试中占据主导。

questions.stem: What does a new study from Stanford show about the importance of passion in predicting achievement?

options.A: It reflects a strong sense of obligation to others.
options.B: It signifies a universal model of motivation.
options.C: It may differ in various cultures.
options.D: It may have been underestimated.

questions.cn: 斯坦福大学的这项新研究就“热情在预测成就中的作用”显示了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它体现出强烈的对他人的责任感。
optionsCn.B: 它标志着一种普适的动机模式。
optionsCn.C: 它在不同文化中可能有所不同。
optionsCn.D: 它可能一直被低估了。

questions.stem: What did the researchers find about the effect of passion on academic achievement for those in more collectivistic societies?

options.A: It was under-investigated.
options.B: It was more predictable.
options.C: It was taken for granted.
options.D: It was more subtle.

questions.cn: 关于热情对集体主义色彩更强的社会中人们学业成就的影响，研究者发现了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它受到的考察不足。
optionsCn.B: 它更可预测。
optionsCn.C: 它被视为理所当然。
optionsCn.D: 它更为细微。

lines.t: In America, at least, passion is a word that often comes up on job descriptions and in interviews.
lines.cn: 至少在美国，passion（热情）是职位描述和面试里经常出现的一个词。

lines.t: On the whole, passionate people are thought of in a positive light and considered likely to achieve their goals.
lines.cn: 总的来说，人们正面看待充满热情的人，认为他们更可能实现目标。

lines.t: But when it comes to predicting achievement, has the importance of passion been overstated?
lines.cn: 但说到预测成就，热情的重要性是不是被夸大了？

lines.t: According to a new study from Stanford University, passion may be less important in certain cultures.
lines.cn: 斯坦福大学一项新研究显示，在某些文化中，热情或许没那么重要。

lines.t: And the fact that passion is often seen as a key to achievement may reflect a distinctly Western model of motivation.
lines.cn: 而热情常被视为成就的关键，这一现象可能反映的是一种典型的西方动机模式。

lines.t: The chief factor explored in the study was how individualistic a society was.
lines.cn: 该研究考察的核心因素是社会的个人主义程度。

lines.t: In individualistic cultures, the researchers assert, people are more motivated by pursuing paths related to their passions.
lines.cn: 研究者指出，在个人主义文化中，人们更多是被追随自身热爱的道路所驱动。

lines.t: But those in collectivistic cultures are more likely to see themselves as part of a network.
lines.cn: 而在集体主义文化中，人们更可能把自己看作一个关系网络的一部分。

lines.t: They often place fulfilling obligations to others above focusing on their own interests.
lines.cn: 他们往往把履行对他人的义务置于关注自身利益之上。

lines.t: The researchers looked at data from nearly 60 countries.
lines.cn: 研究者分析了近 60 个国家的数据。

lines.t: They found that, in science subjects, passion was positively correlated with academic achievements.
lines.cn: 他们发现，在理科科目中，热情与学业成绩呈正相关。

lines.t: Higher levels of enjoyment and interest also bolstered test scores.
lines.cn: 更高的愉悦感和兴趣水平也提升了考试成绩。

lines.t: But the strength of this correlation wasn't the same across cultures.
lines.cn: 但这种相关性的强度在不同文化之间并不相同。

lines.t: Those in individualistic societies, such as the US, Australia, and the UK, showed a stronger link between passion and achievement.
lines.cn: 在美国、澳大利亚、英国等个人主义社会，热情与成就之间的联系更强。

lines.t: The effect of passion on performance was more subtle for those in more collectivistic societies such as Colombia or Thailand.
lines.cn: 而在哥伦比亚、泰国等集体主义色彩更强的社会，热情对表现的影响更为细微。

lines.t: These findings were mirrored in achievement in both mathematics and reading.
lines.cn: 这些发现在数学和阅读成绩上都得到了印证。

lines.t: It's clear from the findings that passion isn't the only thing that motivates people to achieve their goals.
lines.cn: 研究结果清楚表明，热情并不是激励人们实现目标的唯一因素。

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the passage say is a pattern in nature?

options.A: It is any incidental happening in plants and animals or ice crystals.
options.B: It is any basic physical or chemical work in designing substances.
options.C: It is any symmetrical and colorful stripes or spots on organisms.
options.D: It is any regularly repeated arrangement of shapes or colors.

questions.cn: 文章说自然界中的图案是什么？

optionsCn.A: 它是动植物或冰晶中偶然发生的事。
optionsCn.B: 它是设计物质时所做的任何基础物理或化学工作。
optionsCn.C: 它是生物体上任何对称而多彩的条纹或斑点。
optionsCn.D: 它是形状或颜色有规律重复出现的排列。

questions.stem: What gives rise to complex patterns at a larger scale?

options.A: Materials undergoing certain processes.
options.B: Materials exposed to various natural forces.
options.C: Materials impacted by any change of molecules.
options.D: Materials going through extremely radical transformations.

questions.cn: 是什么在更大尺度上产生了复杂的图案？

optionsCn.A: 经历某些过程的材料。
optionsCn.B: 暴露于各种自然力之下的材料。
optionsCn.C: 受任何分子变化影响的材料。
optionsCn.D: 经历极其剧烈转变的材料。

questions.stem: What does the example of frozen crystals on a window show?

options.A: The beauty of molecular clustering.
options.B: The way for appreciating patterns.
options.C: The creation of patterns.
options.D: The factors affecting clusters.

questions.cn: 窗户上冰晶的例子说明了什么？

optionsCn.A: 分子聚集之美。
optionsCn.B: 欣赏图案的方法。
optionsCn.C: 图案的形成。
optionsCn.D: 影响团簇的因素。

questions.stem: What might molecular processes produce, according to the passage?

options.A: A pattern by accident.
options.B: Patterns for specific purposes.
options.C: Patterns with random imperfections.
options.D: A pattern with artificial intervention.

questions.cn: 根据文章，分子过程可能产生什么？

optionsCn.A: 偶然形成的图案。
optionsCn.B: 有特定用途的图案。
optionsCn.C: 带有随机瑕疵的图案。
optionsCn.D: 需要人工干预的图案。

lines.t: Why does nature create patterns?
lines.cn: 大自然为什么会形成图案？

lines.t: The reason patterns often appear in nature is simple.
lines.cn: 大自然中图案频繁出现，原因其实很简单。

lines.t: The same basic physical or chemical processes occur in many patterned substances and organisms as they form.
lines.cn: 许多有图案的物质和生物在形成时，都经历了相同的基本物理或化学过程。

lines.t: Whether in plants and animals or rocks, foams, and ice crystals, the intricate patterns that happen in nature come down to what's happening at the level of atoms and molecules.
lines.cn: 无论是在动植物中，还是在岩石、泡沫和冰晶中，大自然里那些精巧的图案都归结于原子和分子层面发生的变化。

lines.t: A pattern in nature is any regularly repeated arrangement of shapes or colors.
lines.cn: 自然界中的图案，指的是形状或颜色有规律地重复出现的排列。

lines.t: Some of the most striking examples include the six-sided arrays of rocks at Giant's Causeway in the United Kingdom and the colorful stripes and spots on tropical fish.
lines.cn: 最引人注目的例子包括英国巨人堤道的六边形石柱群，以及热带鱼身上色彩斑斓的条纹和斑点。

lines.t: Patterns like these begin to form at a small scale when materials undergo processes like drying, freezing, wrinkling, diffusing, and reacting.
lines.cn: 这类图案始于小尺度：当材料经历干燥、冻结、起皱、扩散和反应等过程时便会出现。

lines.t: These changes then give rise to complex patterns at a larger scale that people can see.
lines.cn: 这些变化随后在大尺度上形成人眼可见的复杂图案。

lines.t: Imagine delicate frozen crystals on a window during winter.
lines.cn: 想象一下冬天窗户上那些精致的冰晶。

lines.t: What creates that pattern?
lines.cn: 是什么造就了那样的图案？

lines.t: When water freezes, its molecules begin clustering together.
lines.cn: 水结冰时，其分子开始聚集在一起。

lines.t: Water molecules have a particular bent shape that causes them to stack into clusters as they freeze.
lines.cn: 水分子有一种特殊的弯曲形状，使它们在冻结时堆叠成团簇。

lines.t: As the cluster grows, many outside factors, including humidity and temperature, begin to affect its overall shape.
lines.cn: 随着团簇变大，湿度、温度等许多外部因素开始影响它的整体形状。

lines.t: If the water is freezing on a window, for example, random imperfections on the glass surface affect the stacking and create the larger pattern.
lines.cn: 例如，如果水是在窗户上结冰，玻璃表面随机的瑕疵会影响堆叠方式，从而形成更大的图案。

lines.t: But scientists do not always know the purpose of a pattern, or even if there is one.
lines.cn: 但科学家并不总能知道某个图案的用途，甚至不知道它是否有用途。

lines.t: The molecular processes involved are simple enough that they might generate a pattern by coincidence.
lines.cn: 其中涉及的分子过程足够简单，图案可能只是偶然形成的。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 1 组
tasks.context: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the speaker say is really difficult?

options.A: Eliminating all the old habits at once.
options.B: Making a permanent lifestyle change.
options.C: Realizing all the life goals one has set.
options.D: Improving multiple areas of one's life.

questions.cn: 讲话者说什么真的很难？

optionsCn.A: 一次戒掉所有旧习惯。
optionsCn.B: 让生活方式发生永久改变。
optionsCn.C: 实现自己设定的所有人生目标。
optionsCn.D: 改善生活的多个方面。

questions.stem: What did researchers find about people with implementation intentions?

options.A: They were more likely to implement a particular behavior.
options.B: They were more likely to make plans for their future.
options.C: They tended to be committed to a single goal.
options.D: They tended to focus on one thing at a time.

questions.cn: 关于有“执行意图”的人，研究者发现了什么？

optionsCn.A: 他们更可能实施某一特定行为。
optionsCn.B: 他们更可能为将来做计划。
optionsCn.C: 他们往往专注于单一目标。
optionsCn.D: 他们往往一次只专注一件事。

questions.stem: According to the speaker, what is required of you when you begin practicing a new habit?

options.A: The ability to make the process automatic.
options.B: A practical timetable for implementation.
options.C: A lot of conscious effort to remember to do it.
options.D: Concentration on the benefits it will provide.

questions.cn: 根据讲话者，开始练习一个新习惯时，需要你具备什么？

optionsCn.A: 让这一过程自动化的能力。
optionsCn.B: 一份切实可行的执行时间表。
optionsCn.C: 记住去做它所需的大量有意识努力。
optionsCn.D: 专注于它将带来的好处。

lines.t: Many people, myself included, have multiple areas of life they would like to improve.
lines.cn: 许多人，包括我自己，都有生活的多个方面想要改善。

lines.t: For example, I would like to reach more people with my writing, to lift heavier weights at the gym, and to start practicing mindfulness more consistently.
lines.cn: 比如，我希望自己的文章能被更多人读到，希望在健身房举起更重的重量，也希望能更坚持地练习正念。

lines.t: Those are just a few of the goals I find desirable, and you probably have a long list yourself.
lines.cn: 这些只是我觉得值得追求的目标中的几个，你大概也有一长串自己的目标。

lines.t: The problem is, even if we are committed to working hard on our goals, our natural tendency is to return to our old habits at some point.
lines.cn: 问题在于，即便我们决心为目标努力，人的天性也会让我们在某个时刻回到旧习惯。

lines.t: Making a permanent lifestyle change is really difficult.
lines.cn: 要让生活方式发生永久改变，真的很难。

lines.t: Recently, I've come across a few studies that will make these difficult lifestyle changes a bit easier.
lines.cn: 最近我看到几项研究，能让这些艰难的生活方式改变变得稍微容易一些。

lines.t: As you'll see, however, the approach to mastering many areas of life is somewhat counter-intuitive.
lines.cn: 不过你会发现，掌握生活诸多方面的方法有点反直觉。

lines.t: Research has shown that you are two to three times more likely to stick with your habits if you make a specific plan for when, where and how you will perform the behaviour.
lines.cn: 研究显示，如果你为某个行为在何时、何地、如何执行制定具体计划，你坚持习惯的可能性会提高两到三倍。

lines.t: For example, in one study, scientists asked people to fill out a sentence to specify during the next week they would do at least 20 minutes of vigorous exercise on which day, at what time of day, and at or in what place.
lines.cn: 例如，在一项研究中，科学家请受试者填写一个句子，明确下周哪一天、一天中的什么时间、在什么地点至少做 20 分钟剧烈运动。

lines.t: Researchers found that people who filled out this sentence were two to three times more likely to actually exercise compared to a control group who did not make plans for their future behaviour.
lines.cn: 研究者发现，填写了这个句子的人，实际去运动的可能性是那些没有为未来行为做计划的对照组的 2 到 3 倍。

lines.t: Psychologists call these specific plans implementation intentions, because they state when, where and how you intend to implement a particular behaviour.
lines.cn: 心理学家把这类具体计划称为“执行意图”，因为它们说明了你想在何时、何地、如何实施某一特定行为。

lines.t: However, follow-up research has discovered implementation intentions only work when you focus on one thing at a time.
lines.cn: 然而，后续研究发现，执行意图只有在你一次只专注一件事时才有效。

lines.t: In fact, researchers found that people who tried to accomplish multiple goals were less committed and less likely to succeed than those who focused on a single goal.
lines.cn: 事实上，研究者发现，试图同时完成多个目标的人，比只专注一个目标的人投入度更低、也更不容易成功。

lines.t: Another science-based reason to focus on one thing at a time is that when you begin practising a new habit, it requires a lot of conscious effort to remember to do it.
lines.cn: 一次只专注一件事的另一个科学理由是：当你开始练习一个新习惯时，记住去做它需要大量的有意识努力。

lines.t: After a while, however, the pattern of behaviour becomes easier.
lines.cn: 不过过一段时间后，这种行为模式会变得容易些。

lines.t: Eventually, your new habit becomes a normal routine and the process is more or less mindless and automatic.
lines.cn: 最终，你的新习惯成为日常惯例，整个过程或多或少变得不假思索、自动完成。

lines.t: The most important thing to note is that there is some tipping point at which new habits become more or less automatic.
lines.cn: 最值得注意的是，存在某个临界点，过了它新习惯就会或多或少变得自动化。

lines.t: The time it takes to build a habit depends on many factors, including how difficult the habit is, your genetics and more.
lines.cn: 养成一个习惯所需的时间取决于许多因素，包括习惯的难度、你的基因等等。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What was one of the more bizarre findings about Pluto's atmosphere?

options.A: It resembles that of Earth in many inconceivable ways.
options.B: It has a haze much thicker than previously believed.
options.C: It is 333.4 °F cooler than earlier estimates.
options.D: It is far beyond any quick measurements.

questions.cn: 关于冥王星大气，比较离奇的发现之一是什么？

optionsCn.A: 它在许多方面不可思议地类似地球大气。
optionsCn.B: 它的霾比先前认为的浓厚得多。
optionsCn.C: 它比早先估计的低 333.4 华氏度。
optionsCn.D: 它远非几次快速测量所能了解。

questions.stem: What is said to determine the overall temperature on Earth?

options.A: The accumulation of solid particles in the air.
options.B: The distribution of gases in its atmosphere.
options.C: The clouds of particles reflecting sun rays.
options.D: The aggravated effects of climate change.

questions.cn: 据说是什么决定了地球的整体温度？

optionsCn.A: 空气中固体颗粒的积聚。
optionsCn.B: 其大气中气体的分布。
optionsCn.C: 反射太阳光线的颗粒云团。
optionsCn.D: 气候变化加剧的影响。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say the researchers have to wait and see?

options.A: If spectrums of light can be better detected by telescope.
options.B: If Pluto's hazy atmosphere can be more easily observed.
options.C: If Pluto's hazy atmosphere scatters strong sunlight.
options.D: If the light from the telescope confirms their idea.

questions.cn: 讲话者说研究者得等着看什么？

optionsCn.A: 望远镜能否更好地探测光谱。
optionsCn.B: 冥王星朦胧的大气能否更容易被观测到。
optionsCn.C: 冥王星朦胧的大气是否散射强烈的阳光。
optionsCn.D: 望远镜捕捉到的光能否验证他们的想法。

lines.t: It was a lazy, hazy, crazy day on the dwarf planet Pluto when New Horizons, a spacecraft from Earth, flew by at a speed of 31,000 miles per hour two years ago.
lines.cn: 两年前，来自地球的“新视野号”探测器以每小时 3.1 万英里的速度飞掠矮行星冥王星，那是个慵懒、朦胧又疯狂的冥王星日。

lines.t: The spacecraft took a bunch of photos, made some quick measurements of Pluto's atmosphere and sent them all back here, giving planetary scientists their first up-close look of the distant dwarf planet.
lines.cn: 这艘探测器拍了一大堆照片，对冥王星大气做了些快速测量，并把它们全部传回地球，让行星科学家第一次近距离观察这颗遥远的矮行星。

lines.t: One of the more bizarre things they found was that the haze in Pluto's atmosphere was much thicker than previously thought.
lines.cn: 他们发现的比较离奇的现象之一是：冥王星大气中的霾比之前认为的要浓厚得多。

lines.t: The planet also had an atmosphere much cooler than earlier estimates, topping out at minus 333.4 degrees Fahrenheit.
lines.cn: 这颗行星的大气也比早先的估计冷得多，最高温度只有华氏零下 333.4 度。

lines.t: Now a study published in Nature links those two atmospheric observations.
lines.cn: 如今，发表在《自然》杂志上的一项研究把这两项大气观测结果联系了起来。

lines.t: A computer model developed by planetary scientist Xi Zang and colleagues shows the haze of tiny droplets in the upper atmosphere is likely scattering light from the sun, preventing heat from reaching the planet below.
lines.cn: 行星科学家臧希及其同事开发的计算机模型显示，高层大气中由微小液滴构成的霾很可能散射了来自太阳的光，使热量无法到达下方的行星表面。

lines.t: We see hazy skies on Earth too from time to time, whenever solid particles get suspended in the air, from water-based fogs to ash from fires to the toxic droplets that make up a thick smog.
lines.cn: 地球上偶尔也会出现朦胧的天空：只要固体颗粒悬浮在空气中就会如此——从水雾，到火灾产生的灰烬，再到构成浓厚雾霾的有毒液滴。

lines.t: But on Earth the overall temperature of the planet is dominated by the distribution of gases in our atmosphere.
lines.cn: 但在地球上，行星的整体温度主要由大气中气体的分布决定。

lines.t: On Pluto, the authors suggest, haze might be more influential.
lines.cn: 作者提出，在冥王星上，霾的影响可能更大。

lines.t: Particles can reflect light from the sun here on Earth.
lines.cn: 在地球上，颗粒也能反射来自太阳的光。

lines.t: It happens after volcanoes erupt, emitting clouds of particles that reflect the sun's rays into the atmosphere.
lines.cn: 火山喷发后就会出现这种情况：喷出的颗粒云团把太阳光线反射到大气中。

lines.t: Some people even propose imitating this phenomenon to alleviate the effects of climate change.
lines.cn: 有人甚至提出模仿这一现象来缓解气候变化的影响。

lines.t: But our planet isn't dominated by that process, or at least it hasn't been for a few billion years.
lines.cn: 但我们这颗行星并不由这一过程主导，至少几十亿年来都不是。

lines.t: If Pluto's atmosphere is very different from ours, and from that of other nearby planets, it could help scientists expand their understanding of planetary atmospheres.
lines.cn: 如果冥王星的大气与地球以及附近其他行星的大气非常不同，那它可能有助于科学家拓展对行星大气的认识。

lines.t: But right now this is just a good guess, based on data from New Horizons and a sophisticated computer model, not direct observations of the haze's composition.
lines.cn: 但眼下这还只是个合理的推测，依据是“新视野号”的数据和一个精密的计算机模型，而不是对霾成分的直接观测。

lines.t: There are other theories floating around to explain Pluto's cool temperatures, including blaming the cold air on gases in the atmosphere.
lines.cn: 还有其他一些理论在流传，用来解释冥王星的低温，包括把冷空气归因于大气中的气体。

lines.t: Luckily, the authors will get a chance to test their notions when the James Webb Space Telescope launches later.
lines.cn: 幸运的是，等詹姆斯·韦布空间望远镜日后发射升空，作者们将有机会检验他们的设想。

lines.t: That observatory can detect different spectrums of light, which the hazy Plutonian atmosphere would be positively glowing with, as it's scattered sunlight.
lines.cn: 那座天文台能够探测不同光谱的光，而朦胧的冥王星大气正因为散射了阳光而会明亮地发出这些光。

lines.t: The researchers just have to wait and see if the light from the telescope validates their bright idea.
lines.cn: 研究者只需等着看望远镜捕捉到的光能否验证他们这个聪明的想法。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 3 组
tasks.context: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What do we learn from the researchers' conclusion at the beginning of the talk?

options.A: Parents can play a decisive role in cultivating their children's musical talent.
options.B: Children are embarrassed by parents' failure to appreciate their music.
options.C: Parents can mould their 8- to 10-year-old children's music taste.
options.D: Children aged 8 to 10 are old enough to produce poetic lyrics.

questions.cn: 从讲座开头研究者的结论中我们能了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 父母能在培养孩子的音乐天赋上起决定性作用。
optionsCn.B: 孩子因父母不欣赏他们的音乐而感到难堪。
optionsCn.C: 父母可以塑造 8 至 10 岁孩子的音乐品味。
optionsCn.D: 8 到 10 岁的孩子已大到能创作富有诗意的歌词。

questions.stem: What does Dr. Hawke Eggerman say about adolescence?

options.A: They start to show their own musical preference.
options.B: They tend to be more influenced by their peers.
options.C: They tend to gravitate away from their homes.
options.D: They are more open to new genres of music.

questions.cn: 关于青春期，霍克·埃格曼博士说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 他们开始表现出自己的音乐偏好。
optionsCn.B: 他们往往更多地受同伴影响。
optionsCn.C: 他们往往想离开家。
optionsCn.D: 他们对新音乐类型更加开放。

questions.stem: What is the key to fostering good taste in later life, according to Dr. Hawke Eggerman?

options.A: Enabling children to be receptive to music experts' suggestions.
options.B: Helping children develop the ability to manage their emotions.
options.C: Familiarising children with different schools of music.
options.D: Introducing children to a variety of musical styles.

questions.cn: 根据霍克·埃格曼博士，培养日后良好品味的关键是什么？

optionsCn.A: 让孩子乐于接受音乐专家的建议。
optionsCn.B: 帮助孩子培养管理情绪的能力。
optionsCn.C: 让孩子熟悉不同的音乐流派。
optionsCn.D: 让孩子接触多种音乐风格。

questions.stem: How can parents help children create positive memories about artists and bands?

options.A: By enhancing children's appreciation of their music.
options.B: By pushing their music hard enough upon children.
options.C: By attending their concerts and live music events with children.
options.D: By introducing their music to children as early as possible.

questions.cn: 父母如何帮助孩子对歌手和乐队留下美好的记忆？

optionsCn.A: 通过增强孩子对他们音乐的欣赏。
optionsCn.B: 通过把他们的音乐足够用力地推给孩子。
optionsCn.C: 通过和孩子一起去看他们的演唱会和现场音乐活动。
optionsCn.D: 通过尽早把他们的音乐介绍给孩子。

lines.t: Parents have a small window where they can influence their 8-10 year old children's music taste, researchers have concluded.
lines.cn: 研究者得出结论：父母有一段很小的窗口期，可以影响 8 到 10 岁孩子的音乐品味。

lines.t: The 24-month time frame comes at an age when youngsters are old enough to appreciate poetic lyrics and snappy tunes, but have not yet started to be embarrassed by their mother and father's preferences.
lines.cn: 这 24 个月的时间窗口正好出现在这样一个年龄段：孩子已经大到能欣赏富有诗意的歌词和轻快的旋律，但还没开始因父母的喜好而感到难堪。

lines.t: Dr. Hawke Eggerman, a lecturer in music at the University of York, carried out a literature review into more than a dozen studies looking at parental musical influence.
lines.cn: 约克大学音乐讲师霍克·埃格曼博士对十几项考察父母音乐影响的研究做了文献综述。

lines.t: Children have an openness to new music, and this means parents have an important role to play in developing the musical preferences of their kids, he said.
lines.cn: 他说，孩子对新音乐持开放态度，这意味着父母在孩子音乐偏好的形成中扮演着重要角色。

lines.t: However, time is of the essence, as parental influence is most likely to be effective during the critical time period before age 10.
lines.cn: 然而，时间至关重要，因为父母的影响最可能在 10 岁之前这段关键时期内奏效。

lines.t: During adolescence, children tend to gravitate away from their parents' choices and are more influenced by their peers.
lines.cn: 到了青春期，孩子往往会偏离父母的选择，更多地受同伴影响。

lines.t: A separate survey of 2,000 British parents by music streaming service, Deezer, also found that nearly four-fifths of parents agreed that their children were far more receptive to their musical suggestions before the age of 10.
lines.cn: 音乐流媒体服务 Deezer 对 2000 名英国父母所做的另一项调查也发现，近五分之四的父母认同：孩子 10 岁前对他们的音乐建议要容易接受得多。

lines.t: In contrast, just 10% of parents reported positive reactions from their teenage children when they shared their favourite music.
lines.cn: 相比之下，只有 10% 的父母说，他们分享自己最爱的音乐时，十几岁的孩子给出了积极反应。

lines.t: Some 79% of fathers said they had tried to influence their children's music, but just 69% of mothers.
lines.cn: 约 79% 的父亲说他们尝试过影响孩子的音乐品味，母亲则为 69%。

lines.t: However, mothers were more effective, with 38% reporting that their kids loved the tunes they shared, compared to 30% of dads who in some cases said their children cried or even fell asleep.
lines.cn: 不过母亲更有效：38% 的母亲说孩子喜欢自己分享的曲子，而父亲只有 30%——有些父亲还说孩子听了哭了，甚至睡着了。

lines.t: Dr. Eggerman claims introducing children to a variety of musical styles is the key to fostering good taste in later life.
lines.cn: 埃格曼博士称，让孩子接触多种音乐风格是培养日后良好品味的关键。

lines.t: By playing children a variety of genres before this critical period, research on familiarization suggests they will enjoy lots of different types of music as adults he added.
lines.cn: 他补充说，在这一关键期之前给孩子播放多种类型的音乐，关于熟悉化的研究表明，他们成年后会喜欢上许多不同类型的音乐。

lines.t: The benefits of having a wider taste in music include the ability to manage their emotions more effectively, socialise and bond with others more easily, and to have a better understanding of other cultures as well.
lines.cn: 音乐品味更广的好处包括：能更有效地管理情绪、更容易与人交往和建立情感联系，也能更好地理解其他文化。

lines.t: Dr. Eggerman advises parents not to push their favourite music too hard on their children, but instead play it as background music while a child is playing.
lines.cn: 埃格曼博士建议父母不要把自己的音乐强加给孩子，而是趁孩子玩耍时把它当作背景音乐播放。

lines.t: They can also help create positive memories about artists and bands by going to concerts and live music events together.
lines.cn: 父母还可以通过一起去看演唱会和现场音乐活动，帮助孩子对歌手和乐队留下美好的记忆。
